investigation.title: session-share-public-read eval timeout: anonymous public share endpoint returned no evidence in desktop-release
investigation.summary: The session-share-public-read eval for the project-agent-workflows feature timed out after 37926ms on desktop-nightly-macos-aarch64, producing an empty evidence object and failing all 7 required evidence assertions. The upstream chat-stream step (project-agent-chat-stream) passed cleanly in the same run, isolating the failure to the share-creation or anonymous public-read leg of the probe.
investigation.rootCause: The eval runner reached the session-share-public-read probe branch (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1273-1278), successfully completed the prerequisite runProjectChatTurn step (evidenced by the passing project-agent-chat-stream sibling), but then timed out waiting for a response from the anonymous public share endpoint before any of the required evidence fields (shareIdPresent, shareUrlPresent, publicMessageCount, projectId, agentInstanceId, sessionId, textSample) could be populated. The most likely locus is the share-creation API call or the subsequent anonymous public-read request hanging or returning an error that the probe did not surface before the 30000ms internal timeout expired. This is an eval-layer failure against the desktop-release runtime environment; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the evidence to indicate a production outage.

failed-check.evidence: empty object {} — zero evidence keys were captured, meaning the share creation or public read step produced no usable response.

sibling.project-agent-chat-stream: status=pass, latencyMs=6917, evidenceKeys include projectId, agentInstanceId, sessionId, textSample — the prerequisite chat turn succeeded, ruling out a shared upstream dependency failure.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:133-141: contract requires shareIdPresent=true and shareUrlPresent=true, neither of which was returned.
possibleCauses: The anonymous public share endpoint (called after runProjectChatTurn) is slow or unresponsive in the desktop-release environment, causing the probe to exhaust its 30000ms internal timeout before receiving shareIdPresent or shareUrlPresent.
The share-creation API call returned an error (e.g. 4xx/5xx) that the probe runner treated as a hang rather than an immediate failure, consuming the full timeout budget.

A regression introduced by commit dfbc1b6 ('fix(observability): align live probe fixtures') may have altered probe fixture configuration or workflow setup in a way that affects how the share endpoint is reached or authenticated — this is a low-confidence hypothesis because dfbc1b6's touched paths are CI/workflow files and do not include candidate code paths matching the share logic needles.

The eval harness access token (args.token) was present (otherwise the probe would have returned SKIP, not a timeout), but the token may lack the permission scope required to create or read a public share, causing the share API to hang or reject silently.

A network or environment-level issue specific to desktop-nightly-macos-aarch64 caused the share endpoint request to stall; the chat-stream sibling passed quickly (6917ms) suggesting the base API is reachable, but the share endpoint may route differently.

investigation.title: Remote Agent Creation Eval Failing: POST /api/agents Returns 409 Agent Quota Exceeded (limit is 100)
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-06-15T23:00:45–48Z with an identical 409 conflict response from POST /api/agents: "conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100". The eval probe account's organization has reached the swarm agent hard limit of 100, preventing the observability runner from creating a new remote agent and causing all required evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) to go uncollected.
investigation.rootCause: The swarm backend rejected POST /api/agents with HTTP 409 and error code "conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100", meaning the probe org has accumulated 100 remote agents and the backend enforces a hard cap at that number. Because agent creation is the first step in the eval runner branch (run-status-probes.mjs line 1312: createAgent(args, track, "remote", null, orgId)), no agent was created, no evidence was written, and all downstream assertions against vmIdPresent and remoteState could not be evaluated. This is an eval infrastructure failure caused by a resource exhaustion condition in the probe org, not a general product outage for end users.

possibleCauses: PRIMARY — Probe org has hit the swarm agent hard quota of 100: a prior eval run (or runs) created agents that were not cleaned up, accumulating until the limit was reached. The withCleanup wrapper in the runner (run-status-probes.mjs line 1310) is responsible for deleting agents after each run; if cleanup failed or was skipped in a previous run, leaked agents would accumulate toward the cap.
SECONDARY — The eval runner's cleanup path (withCleanup / track) failed silently in one or more prior runs, leaving orphaned remote agents in the probe org that count against the quota.
TERTIARY — The probe org's agent quota was reduced (e.g., by a backend config change) to a value already exceeded by existing agents, causing new creation attempts to fail immediately.

investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-state, remote-agent-create, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-06-15T23:00:46–48Z with an identical 409 conflict response from POST /api/agents: the swarm backend rejected agent creation because the org-scoped agent quota of 100 has been reached. Because agent creation is the first step in the eval runner (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1332: createAgent), no subsequent state-polling or runtime steps could execute, leaving all required evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) uncollected. This is an eval-infrastructure failure against the production-api endpoint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the packet to confirm a broader user-facing outage.
investigation.rootCause: The production-api swarm backend returned HTTP 409 with error code "conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100" on every attempt by the eval runner to call POST /api/agents. The eval probe for remote-agent-state calls createAgent as its first action (run-status-probes.mjs:1332); when that call fails with a non-retryable 409, the probe exits immediately without writing any evidence, causing the contract validation to report all four required fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) as missing. The same upstream failure propagated identically to the sibling checks remote-agent-create and remote-agent-runtime, confirming the failure is at the shared agent-creation dependency rather than in any check-specific logic.

A prior eval run crashed or was interrupted before its withCleanup handler could delete the agent it created, leaving a leaked agent that incrementally consumed quota over multiple runs until the limit was reached.

investigation.title: Image Generation Stream Eval Failure: GENERATION_NO_EVENTS Error Terminates Stream Before completion_completed Frame or Artifact URL
investigation.summary: The eval check `image-generation-stream` on `desktop-release` / `desktop-nightly-macos-aarch64` failed because the SSE stream emitted a `generation_error` frame with code `GENERATION_NO_EVENTS` before ever producing a `generation_completed` frame or an artifact URL. Both required evidence keys (`frameTypes` containing `generation_completed`, and `imageUrlPresent: true`) are entirely absent from the captured frame sequence, causing the expected-output contract defined in `infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json` (lines 267–273) to be fully unmet. This is an eval-layer failure reflecting a real backend stream termination; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the packet.
investigation.rootCause: The `/api/generate/image/stream` endpoint (called by the runner at `infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs` line 1411) stopped emitting SSE events mid-generation and the server-side watchdog emitted a `generation_error` frame with code `GENERATION_NO_EVENTS` and message "Image generation stopped sending progress before completing." The stream never reached the `generation_completed` event, so the runner's evidence write at line 1425 (`imageUrlPresent: Boolean(imageUrl)`) produced no artifact URL and `frameTypes` never contained `generation_completed`. The exact cause of the upstream stall is uncertain from the available evidence — it could be a transient upstream model API timeout, a server-side event-pump hang, or a resource/quota issue on the image generation backend — but the observable failure boundary is the `/api/generate/image/stream` endpoint failing to complete the generation job within the eval window.
